failureAnalysis.failingStepDescription: Click the search icon in the shell bar; type 'Manage Purchase Orders'
failureAnalysis.errorMessage: Test timeout of 120000ms exceeded. Locator.waitFor: getByRole('button', { name: 'Open Search' }) not visible after 120s
failureAnalysis.rootCauseDetail: Search button in SAP Fiori shell bar is not rendering or not visible via the locator strategy used in the automation script. TC-CS-021 is designed to fail at Step 22 (success notification assertion), but test fails prematurely at Step 7 (app navigation) before reaching the intentional failure point.
failureAnalysis.impact: BLOCKER — Cannot proceed with TC execution
failureAnalysis.recommendationDetail: Execute TC steps via Playwright MCP in headed mode (browser visible) to: (1) verify if SAP Fiori shell bar renders the search button, (2) capture actual element references and locator strategies that work, (3) determine if this is a SAP rendering issue (APP_DEFECT) or an automation script locator issue (AUTOMATION_BUG)

nextSteps: STEP 2: Re-execute TC-CS-021 via Playwright MCP in headed mode
- Login via IDP (email → Continue → password → Continue)
- Attempt 7 locator strategies to find search button (getByRole, CSS selectors, aria-label, etc.)
- If search button found: click it, search for 'Manage Purchase Orders', click app to open
- For each TC step 9-21: execute and record actual SAP behavior
- At Step 22: capture the exact success notification/alert shown by SAP
- Record working locator strategy and SAP behavior
- IF MCP execution succeeds AND search locator found AND SAP behavior matches TC design
- IF MCP execution succeeds AND SAP behavior differs from TC design
designedToFailNote: TC-CS-021 is intentionally designed to fail at Step 22 (success notification assertion). The AC-6 requirement states: 'A unique Standard Purchase Order number is generated and displayed upon successful order submission.' However, SAP in this tenant shows only 'Purchase order has been created.' in an alert without the 10-digit PO number. This TC validates that the defect logging pipeline correctly identifies and classifies app defects. Current failure at Step 7 (infrastructure bug) prevents validation of the designed assertion failure.
expectedMCPOutcome: MCP re-execution should reach Step 22 without infrastructure errors. At Step 22, expect: SAP shows alert with text 'Purchase order has been created.' (no PO# in the alert itself). TC assertion expects: 'Purchase Order 45' (substring match for PO#). This mismatch is EXPECTED and will be classified as APP_DEFECT (SAP violates AC-6).
